bar.defaults.notes: Industry rules of thumb, editable in the tools. Pour cost targets: blended 18–24%, liquor 15–20%, draught 20–25%, wine by the glass 26–32% (bar-industry guides). Draught: 95%+ keg yield achievable (Bar-i, ~200 audits a month, 2018). Espresso: INEI certified single 7 g ± 0.5 for 25 ml; SCA 2017 survey: over 75% of baristas use 18 g double baskets. Coffee waste about 10% (roaster estimate). Milk waste: cafés commonly lose 10–20% of milk bought (vendor estimates); 10% default.

value.draughtWasteBasis: A well-run draught system sells 95% or more of each keg (Bar-i audits of US bars); weeks with line cleaning lose about 2 points more, and bars that don't track it often lose 15–25%.

value.pourCostBasis: Many bars aim for 18–24% overall: spirits about 15–20%, draught beer 20–25%, wine by the glass 26–32%.

manager.forecast.notes: Sales forecast and prep list: weights for the same weekday in the last four weeks, newest first ((W1×1 + W2×2 + W3×3 + W4×4) ÷ 10 with W4 the newest, as Mise gives it), and the buffer added to prep amounts (Mise: add 10–20% on perishables after subtracting stock on hand). An empty week is skipped and its weight is shared out over the others. Event and weather adjustments are the user's own % and multiply the average, as in Mise's worked example (festival ×1.3, rain on a terrace ×0.85). Industry method, not law.

manager.tipOut.notes: Common tip-out shares in US restaurants, set by each house (no legal standard). By % of tips: bussers 10–30%, bartenders 10–20%, runners 5–10%, hosts 3–5%; overall about 20–30% of tips. opening.contingency.notes: Contingency for overruns, as a % of the setup costs (everything except the working capital reserve and the contingency itself). Guides say 10–20% of the budget and 10–15% on build-out; Restaurant Calculator suggests 10%, and 15% for a bare shell, where overruns are most likely. opening.guide.notes: Used by every country. Usual share of the total opening cost (including the working capital reserve and contingency) per budget group and concept. No source publishes all twelve groups by concept: the ranges are Restaurant Calculator's estimate, anchored to the survey's medians (construction about half, kitchen and bar equipment a fifth to a third, pre-opening and training about 5%) and the guides' ranges (build-out 30–40%, equipment 15–25%, deposits 5–10%, permits 2–5%, working capital 15–20%). Service, menu and space factors multiply a group's share relative to what the concept already assumes (baseService, baseSpace); deposits also scale by the country's rent.moveIn deposit + advance months ÷ baseDepositMonths. Then all groups are scaled so the midpoints add up to 100% and bounds are rounded to whole percents (OpeningMath.guide).
